page.layout: One printed page (page 89) with a single text column of running text; marginal dates and notes in the left margin beside the text (years 1588, 1590, 1546, 1548, 1552, 1556); a marginal note "Commonitio" and "pro Trin-cipibus" in the right margin; a line-final signature "F 5" at the foot.

main_text.p: Mompelgardico, cum in Henrici III. Galliae Regis vitam insuper consspirasset, confossus: Jacobus Marchio Badensis, apostata; qui Pontificiam religionem in ditionibus suas reducturus, ipso die Ecclesiarum confessionis deputato, dysenteria correptus, animam efflavit. 1588. Neque vero solum naturali aut violenta morte Deus Regibus, vasallis suis foedifragis, regnum eripit; sed & de sede eos depositurus, infelicitate eventuum & errore in consiliis punit: ut nolentes volentes, imperio relicto, coenobiis se includant. Exemplo sunt ex Graecis Impp. Michael Curopalates, Isacius Comnenus, Michael Ducas: ex Germanis solus Carolus V. ante bellum Germanicum, Papae & Pontificiorum instinctu religionis ergo motum in Joannem Fridericum Electorem Saxonem & Philippum Hassiae Landgravium, fortissimus & victoriosissimus: sed qui rerum gestarum succeisu factus confidentior, cum in armatis Comitiis Augustanis Pontificiam Interreligionis formulam Protestantibus Imperii Principibus & Statibus obtruderet: suam fortunam paulo post subito mutari videns (Meti siquidem Imperiali urbe amissa, hinc a Mauricio Electore & Foederatis Principibus Oenipontefugato, Passaviae randem religionis pax ipsi est extorta) Imperio Electoribus resignato, omniumque regnorum & provinciarum Belgicarum gubernatione traditae Philippo filio, in Hispania se coenobio inclusit. 1590. De qua vitae Caesaris commutatione tale extat epigramma;

p.i: Caesar eram: Theatinus ero. Do robur & arma Petro: ut sit frater, qui Theatinus erat.
Imperii tibi, Frater, onus; tibi regna, Philippe,

main_text.p: Hoc flosculo & his exemplis admoniti Reges & Principes, quod regnant, id totum soli Deo Regum Regi Opt. Max. acceptum referant: seque ejus ministros, clientes, beneficiarios, & vasallos cum debita animi submissione agnoscant: cumque cum timore & tremore colant & revereantur: nec tributum ipsi suum, cultum nempe divinum, aut intercipiant aut avertere co-Commonitio pro Trinitate.

page.notes: Marginal dates in the left margin: 1588, 1590, 1546, 1548, 1552, 1556, placed beside their lines as printed; the exact line of each date is approximate. Several words in the text are doubtful and are not marked individually: "Interreligionis formulam" and "succeisu" (likely "successu"), "Passaviae randem" (likely "Passaviae tandem"), "Meti" (likely "Mariae/Metis"), "Ducas" and "Carolus" as printed. The Latin verse lines "Caesar eram" and "Imperii tibi" are reproduced from the scan as best legible; the page is set in a faded and damaged state, so letters in the middle of several lines are uncertain. The right margin shows the marginal notes "Commonitio" and "pro Trin-cipibus", which are partially cut and illegible at the line ends. The final line of text is cut at the foot and continues on the following page.
